description: Representing and transforming time series, moving-window statistics, ARMA-family model estimation and forecasting, and simulation and analysis of random processes including Markov chains and continuous-time processes.

tools.name: TimeSeries
tools.description: Represents a sequence of values indexed by times or dates, with built-in handling of resampling, missing values and units. It can be constructed from value/time pairs, from values plus a date specification, or from imported data. Most statistics and plotting functions accept it directly.
tools.usage:
TimeSeries[{{t1, v1}, {t2, v2}, ...}]
TimeSeries[values, {tstart, tend, dt}]

parameters.name: ResamplingMethod
parameters.description: How values between samples are interpolated, e.g. {"Interpolation", InterpolationOrder -> 1}.

tools.notes: TemporalData generalizes TimeSeries to several paths or components; EventSeries treats data as discrete events without interpolation.

tools.name: TemporalData
tools.description: Represents one or many time-indexed paths, such as an ensemble of simulated trajectories or multivariate measurements. It supports path selection, slicing and component extraction. RandomFunction returns its results in this form.
tools.usage:
TemporalData[{path1, path2, ...}]
td["PathComponent", k]
td["SliceData", t]

tools.name: TimeSeriesMap
tools.description: Applies a function to the values of a time series while keeping the time stamps unchanged. It is the time-series equivalent of Map. Use it for unit conversion, transformation and cleaning.
tools.notes: TimeSeriesMapThread maps across several aligned series at once.

tools.name: TimeSeriesResample
tools.description: Resamples a time series onto a new set of times or a uniform spacing, interpolating as specified by the resampling method. It is essential for aligning series recorded at different rates. Both regular grids and explicit time lists are accepted.
tools.usage:
TimeSeriesResample[ts, dt]
TimeSeriesResample[ts, {tmin, tmax, dt}]
TimeSeriesResample[ts, times]

tools.name: TimeSeriesShift
tools.description: Shifts all time stamps of a time series by a given amount, without changing the values. Use it to align series that are offset in time or to build lagged predictors. The shift may be a number or a time quantity.

tools.name: TimeSeriesWindow
tools.description: Extracts the part of a time series lying within a specified time interval. It is the standard way to zoom in on a period of interest. Date objects and plain numbers are both accepted.

tools.name: TimeSeriesAggregate
tools.description: Aggregates a time series into coarser intervals, applying a function such as Mean or Total to the values in each bin. Interval specifications can be calendar units like "Month" or "Year". Use it to turn daily data into monthly summaries.

tools.name: TimeSeriesThread
tools.description: Combines several time series by applying a function to their aligned values, resampling them onto a common time grid first. Use it to add, divide or otherwise combine series recorded independently. The alignment method is configurable.

tools.name: MovingAverage
tools.description: Computes the moving average of a list or time series over a window of given width, or with explicit weights. It is the simplest smoother for trend extraction. The output is shorter than the input unless padding is applied.
tools.notes: MovingMedian is more robust to spikes; ExponentialMovingAverage weights recent values more heavily.

tools.name: MovingMedian
tools.description: Computes the moving median over a sliding window, giving a robust smoother that ignores outliers. It preserves step edges better than a moving average. Use it for noisy sensor data with spikes.
tools.example:
data = RandomReal[1, 100]; data[[50]] = 10;
ListLinePlot[{data, MovingMedian[data, 7]}, PlotRange -> {0, 2}]

tools.name: ExponentialMovingAverage
tools.description: Computes an exponentially weighted moving average with smoothing parameter alpha between 0 and 1. Larger alpha tracks recent changes more closely. It is the standard smoother in finance and control applications.

tools.name: MovingMap
tools.description: Applies an arbitrary function to a sliding window over a list or time series, generalizing moving averages to any statistic. Window size can be given in elements or in time units for date-indexed data. Use it for rolling standard deviations, quantiles and custom indicators.
tools.usage:
MovingMap[f, data, r]
MovingMap[f, ts, wspec]

tools.name: ARProcess
tools.description: Represents an autoregressive process in which each value depends linearly on a fixed number of previous values plus noise. It can be simulated, estimated from data and analyzed symbolically for its correlation and spectrum. Use it as the simplest realistic model of serially correlated data.

tools.name: ARMAProcess
tools.description: Represents an autoregressive moving-average process combining dependence on past values and past noise terms. It captures a wider class of correlation structures than AR alone. Use EstimatedProcess to fit its coefficients to data.

tools.name: ARIMAProcess
tools.description: Represents an ARMA process applied to a differenced series, which handles data with stochastic trends. The differencing order d removes non-stationarity. Use it for economic and business series that drift over time.
tools.notes: SARIMAProcess adds seasonal terms for data with periodic structure.

tools.name: EstimatedProcess
tools.description: Fits the parameters of a specified process family to observed data by maximum likelihood or another method. The result is a fully specified process object ready for forecasting or simulation. Use it as the estimation step of a time-series workflow.

tools.name: TimeSeriesModelFit
tools.description: Automatically selects and fits the best time-series model from a family of candidates such as AR, MA, ARMA, ARIMA and SARIMA. The resulting object reports diagnostics, residuals and information criteria. Use it when you do not want to choose the model order by hand.

tools.name: TimeSeriesForecast
tools.description: Produces forecasts from a fitted process or model object over a specified horizon, optionally with prediction variances. It returns a TimeSeries that can be plotted alongside the historical data. Use it as the final step of forecasting workflows.

tools.name: RandomFunction
tools.description: Simulates one or more sample paths of a random process over a given time range, returning a TemporalData object. Step size and number of paths are specified directly. Use it for Monte Carlo studies of stochastic models.
tools.usage:
RandomFunction[proc, {tmin, tmax, dt}]
RandomFunction[proc, tspec, n]

tools.name: WienerProcess
tools.description: Represents Brownian motion with a given drift and volatility, the fundamental continuous-time stochastic process. It has independent Gaussian increments and continuous paths. Use it as a building block for diffusion models.
tools.notes: GeometricBrownianMotionProcess and OrnsteinUhlenbeckProcess are the common derived diffusions.

tools.name: PoissonProcess
tools.description: Represents a counting process with independent exponentially distributed inter-arrival times at a constant rate. It is the standard model for random arrivals such as customers, photons or failures. Simulated paths are step functions.

tools.name: DiscreteMarkovProcess
tools.description: Represents a discrete-time Markov chain defined by an initial state and a transition matrix. It supports simulation, stationary distribution computation, first-passage times and absorption analysis. Use it for state machines, queuing and reliability models.

tools.name: ContinuousMarkovProcess
tools.description: Represents a continuous-time Markov chain defined by a transition rate matrix. Holding times are exponential and transitions follow the embedded chain. Use it for reliability, epidemiology and chemical kinetics models.

tools.name: StationaryDistribution
tools.description: Computes the long-run stationary distribution of a Markov or other stationary process. For an ergodic chain it gives the fraction of time spent in each state. Use it to find equilibrium behaviour without simulation.

tools.name: HiddenMarkovProcess
tools.description: Represents a hidden Markov model in which an unobserved Markov chain emits observable symbols. It supports likelihood computation, most-likely state sequence decoding and parameter estimation. Use it for speech, bioinformatics and regime-switching models.

tools.name: QueueingProcess
tools.description: Represents a queueing system with specified arrival and service processes and number of servers. Properties give queue length distributions, waiting times and utilization. Use it for capacity planning and service-level analysis.
tools.usage:
QueueingProcess[lambda, mu]
QueueingProcess[arr, serv, c, k]

tools.name: EventSeries
tools.description: Represents time-stamped events where values apply only at their exact times, with no interpolation between them. This differs from TimeSeries, which assumes a continuous underlying signal. Use it for transactions, log entries and discrete observations.

tools.name: TimeSeriesInsert
tools.description: Inserts additional values into a time series at specified times, merging them with the existing data. Later insertions at the same time replace earlier values. Use it to patch or augment a series incrementally.

tools.name: TimeSeriesRescale
tools.description: Rescales the time stamps of a time series onto a new interval while keeping the values unchanged. It is useful for comparing series of different durations on a common normalized axis. The new range is given as a pair of times.
